explain.say: Picture a fun game of tag in the playground. You really want to play, but how do you get in? Look at the first step on the board: watch first. Watching shows you how the game works.

explain.say: Next, wait for a pause, like when a round ends. Jumping into the middle can feel like a crash to the players. Can you spot when a pause might come in a game you know?

explain.say: Now ask kindly: Can I play too? Even better, offer a job, like, I can be the goalie! See that step on the board? People love a helper. What job could you offer?

explain.say: And if they say no? That is okay. The team might be full, and it is not about you. Try again later, or join another game. If someone keeps leaving you out, tell a teacher.

faq.q: What words can I use to join a game?
faq.a: Try: Can I play too? Or: That looks fun, can I join? Offering help works well too: I can keep score!
asks: What do I say to play with other kids?
Tell me about the Ask kindly

faq.q: Why should I wait for a pause?
faq.a: Because stopping a game in the middle can annoy the players. At a pause, they can listen to you and fit you in.
asks: Tell me about the Wait for a pause

faq.q: What if they will not let me join?
faq.a: It can feel sad, and that is okay. Ask another group or try again later. If someone keeps leaving you out on purpose, tell a teacher or another trusted adult.
asks: Tell me about the If they say no

faq.q: What if I do not know the rules?
faq.a: Watch for a minute, or ask: How do you play? Most people like explaining their game.
asks: Tell me about the Watch first

faq.q: Can I start my own game?
faq.a: Yes! Ask: Who wants to play hopscotch? Other children might be waiting for someone to ask.
asks: How do I get others to play with me?

facts: Tag is played all over the world with many names, such as tig in parts of the UK, pega-pega in Brazil and oni-gokko in Japan.
Research on how children join groups found that watching first and then fitting in with the game works better than barging in or changing the rules.

quiz.say: When is the best time to ask to join a game?

options.show: In the middle of a run

options.show: At a pause, like the end of a round

quiz.why: At a pause the players can stop, listen and fit you in.

wrong.0: Mid-run, players cannot listen and may feel interrupted.
wrong.2: Pushing in without asking upsets people.

quiz.say: They say the team is full. What could you do?
quiz.show: The team is full. What now?

quiz.why: Waiting or finding another game keeps everyone friendly.

wrong.0: Pushing in makes the game unfair.
wrong.2: Name-calling hurts and makes things worse.
